meta.title: Telemavix - GPS tracks and telemetry overlays for action cameras | Sefinek
meta.description: Record GPS tracks on your phone and add speed, maps and other data to action camera and drone footage. Discover Telemavix GPS and Telemavix Studio.
meta.keywords: telemavix, telemetry overlay, gps track, fit, gpx, dji osmo action, gopro, dji drone, hud

softwareDescription: Telemavix GPS records routes and phone sensor data. Telemavix Studio adds overlays with speed, maps, tilt and other readings to your videos.
label: Project
heading: Telemavix
intro: Your footage can show more. Use Telemavix Studio to add a speedometer, route map, tilt indicator and other widgets. Customize their appearance, arrange them on your video and show your activity from a new perspective. Use data from your camera or drone, or record your route on your phone with Telemavix GPS.

how.title: How to add telemetry to a video

steps.title: 1. Record your activity
steps.text: Film your activity with an action camera or drone. Use Telemavix GPS alongside it if you want a separate route file or readings from your phone sensors.

steps.title: 2. Open the footage in Studio
steps.text: Start with the original camera file. If it contains telemetry, Studio reads it directly from the footage. You can also add a FIT or GPX file from your phone, sports watch or bike computer. If your DJI drone records telemetry separately, use the flight log from DJI Fly.

steps.title: 3. Add an overlay and save your video
steps.text: If you use a separate telemetry file, check that it lines up with the video. Choose your widgets, arrange them on the footage and check the preview before exporting.

mobile.title: Telemavix GPS for Android
mobile.text: Record your route and phone sensor data even with the screen off. Check speed and distance live and use previously loaded maps offline. Review routes and charts in your history or open FIT or GPX files in Studio. Connect a DJI Osmo Action 4, 5 Pro or 6 over Bluetooth to start logging in the app and filming on the camera with one button. The camera saves your phone's GPS positions in the MP4 file, ready to open in Studio.

desktop.title: Telemavix Studio for your computer
desktop.text: Studio reads telemetry embedded in original MP4 files from supported cameras and drones. You can also sync a FIT or GPX track or a DJI flight log with your video. Choose from over 40 widgets, including a route map, speedometer and tilt indicator. Adjust the overlay in the preview, trim clips and add music. The interface is in Polish and English. The Windows build is regularly tested. Linux and macOS builds are experimental.

download.title: Download Telemavix Studio
download.intro: Choose a package for your operating system and processor. On Windows, the installer is the simplest option. The current version is {{version}}.
download.cpuHelp: Not sure which processor you have? On Windows, go to Settings > System > About and check System type. On Linux and macOS, run `uname -m`: x86_64 means x64, while arm64 or aarch64 means ARM64.
download.runtimeHelp: If you choose the version that requires .NET, install the [.NET 10 Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) for your system and processor. Studio also needs FFmpeg 9 and offers to install it on first launch if it is missing. Linux and macOS versions are experimental.
download.more: All files, checksums and release notes are on the [releases page]({{releasesUrl}}).

overlay.title: Overlay editor with live preview
overlay.text: Drag a speedometer, route map or tilt indicator onto the video. Adjust the size and appearance of your widgets and see the changes immediately in the preview.
overlay.alt: Telemavix Studio preview with a map and speedometer next to the widget panel

timeline.title: Timeline editing
timeline.text: Join clips, cut unwanted sections and add transitions. Use the same timeline to set when widgets appear and adjust the volume of the original audio and music.
timeline.alt: Timeline showing clip thumbnails, marked cuts, an audio waveform and widget layers

telemetry.title: Camera telemetry and GPS tracks
telemetry.text: The summary shows the video settings and available readings, such as distance and top speed. Use an external track as the main source for position and speed, or use it to fill gaps in the camera telemetry.
telemetry.alt: Video settings and telemetry summary next to a route map in the recording preview

devices.title: Supported cameras, drones and Garmin devices
devices.intro: See which devices Studio supports and whether to look for GPS data in the footage, an activity file or a flight log.
devices.note: If your camera does not record GPS positions, you can record your route on your phone with [Telemavix GPS](#apps). With a supported DJI Osmo Action camera, the app can also send your position live for the camera to save in the MP4 file.

rows.notes: Tested models: Action 6 and Action 5 Pro. Other models in the series should work, but have not been tested yet.
rows.gps: The camera saves GPS positions in its MP4 files when it receives them from Telemavix GPS or a DJI GPS Bluetooth remote.

rows.notes: This is the only GoPro model tested so far. Pitch has been checked against recorded footage, while roll still needs a controlled sideways tilt test.
rows.gps: An external FIT or GPX file, for example from Telemavix GPS. The HERO12 Black has no built-in GPS. GPS data from other GoPro models has not yet been verified with real recordings.

rows.notes: Supported models: Mavic Air 2, Mavic 4 Pro, Flip, Avata 360 and Lito X1 Plus.
rows.gps: Mavic Air 2, Mavic 4 Pro, Flip and Avata 360 use a flight log (FlightRecord_*.txt) from DJI Fly. Lito X1 Plus embeds telemetry in the MP4 file.

rows.notes: Tested with the Garmin 7X. Studio also supports FIT files from Garmin bike computers.
rows.gps: A FIT activity file. Studio also reads heart rate, cadence and battery level when present in the file.

rows.notes: Experimental tilt and G-force readings and 360° reframing.
rows.gps: Add GPS data from a FIT or GPX file. Studio does not yet read positions from this camera's footage.
